content:
We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline.

We need 3 reactions: likely (1) amide formation (coupling of carboxylic acid with aniline). (2) Doebner modification to create the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. (3) sulfonamide formation between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and aniline (the phenyl sulfonyl part). But we need to match the target: The sulfonamide attaches to the first phenyl (p-tolyl) and the other phenyl (the one with the unsaturated amide) is attached via sulfonyl group? Actually target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the p-tolyl ring (aniline) and the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl ring (c2...). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) reacting with the aniline of the second phenyl (which is the aniline after amide formation? Wait the second phenyl has an amide attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually the unsaturated amide is C(=O)N attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the second phenyl has an aniline substituent (NH2) at para? The SMILES: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl ring c2 has a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl (aniline). The aniline is attached to the amide nitrogen (N attached to phenyl). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). That phenyl has an NH2 (the N at the end). So the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (the aniline is the amide nitrogen's substituent). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the p-tolyl ring, not to the aniline.

Thus retrosynthesis: Step 1 (forward) amide formation: carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) + aniline (c3ccccc3N) -> unsaturated amide. So retrosynthetic disconnection: break C-N amide bond to give acid and aniline.

Step 2: Doebner modification to make the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl ring c2 with aldehyde) and malonic acid. So break C=C double bond and decarboxylate to give aldehyde and malonic acid.

Step 3: Sulfonamide formation: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride + aniline (the phenyl ring c2 with sulfonyl attached) -> sulfonamide. Wait the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to p-tolyl, not to the phenyl c2. Actually the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the nitrogen attached to p-tolyl is the sulfonamide nitrogen, and the sulfonyl group attached to phenyl c2. So the sulfonamide formation would be between p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (p-CH3C6H4SO2Cl) and the aniline of the p-tolyl ring? No, the nitrogen is part of the p-tolyl ring (an aniline). So we need p-toluidine (p-methyl aniline) reacting with sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl (c2...). Actually the sulfonyl chloride would be derived from the second phenyl (c2) with sulfonyl chloride attached to it (c2S(=O)(=O)Cl). Then reacting with p-toluidine gives the sulfonamide linking them. So retrosynthetic step: break S-N bond to give p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So we need to generate aryl sulfonyl chloride from the phenyl c2 (maybe via chlorosulfonation of that phenyl). But we have only 3 steps total, so we need to combine steps: maybe we consider sulfonamide formation as final step, amide formation as second, Doebner as first. That's 3 steps.

Thus we need to produce a JSON tree: root molecule target, children: reaction 1 (sulfonamide formation) with template id for sulfonamide formation, children: two precursors: p-toluidine (SMILES: Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (SMILES: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2). Then reaction 2 (amide formation) applied to the aryl sulfonyl chloride? Wait the aryl sulfonyl chloride is part of the target after sulfonamide formation; but the amide formation is on the side chain attached to that phenyl. So the aryl sulfonyl chloride precursor still contains the side chain unsaturated acid? Actually the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the phenyl ring with sulfonyl chloride and the side chain unsaturated acid (still present). So we need to define the precursor for reaction 2 as the same phenyl with side chain unsaturated acid but with sulfonyl chloride instead of sulfonamide. So we need to generate that molecule: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 with side chain /C=C/C(=O)OH (the acid). The side chain after amide formation is unsaturated amide; before amide formation it's unsaturated acid. So the precursor for amide formation is the unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl chloride. Its SMILES: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2/C=C/C(=O)O (maybe). Let's construct: aromatic phenyl with sulfonyl chloride and side chain: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2/C=C/C(=O)O. Add appropriate aromatic ring: "c1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1/C=C/C(=O)O". That's the unsaturated acid.

Then reaction 2 (amide formation) disconnection: break amide bond to give acid (the above unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the precursor for amide formation is the unsaturated acid (as above) and aniline (c1ccccc1N). Actually the aniline is "c1ccccc1N". So reaction 2 children: unsaturated acid and aniline.

Reaction 3 (Doebner) disconnection: unsaturated acid derived from aldehyde + malonic acid. So break C=C double bond to give aromatic aldehyde (c1ccc(C=O)cc1) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). The side chain attaches at the aldehyde carbon. So the aldehyde precursor is the phenyl ring (same as the phenyl with sulfonyl chloride) but with aldehyde instead of side chain: c1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1C=O. That's the aldehyde.

Thus final tree: target -> reaction (sulfonamide formation) -> precursors: p-toluidine and intermediate1 (aryl sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated acid). That intermediate1 -> reaction (amide formation) -> precursors: unsaturated acid (aryl sulfonyl chloride with acid) and aniline. The unsaturated acid -> reaction (Doebner) -> precursors: aldehyde (aryl sulfonyl chloride aldehyde) and malonic acid.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We can search for sulfonamide formation template. Let's search for functional groups broken: primary amines and sulfonyl chloride? Actually forward reaction: sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide. So broken: primary amines, sulfonyl chloride; formed: sulfonamides. Let's search.
